answer: A pooled admission bond: each new key posts a deposit, and keys funded from the same treasury are clustered, so the deposit grows with the square of the cluster size. Peers attest each other; if the cluster drifts from the peer median, the whole pool is slashed, not one stake. An honest agent risks a modest bond, while an attacker wanting a thousand voices must lock a thousand squared deposits and lose them at the first dishonest round. Each clone raises the price of the next, so no spiral of free identities. That gap is the defense: a fake crystal shatters, a meadow of clones cannot hide.
